public_rationale: On the contextual reading of broadly autonomous device agents, the evidence supports the observation. The January 2024 VisualWebArena evaluation found only 16.4% success for its best agent, compared with 88.7% for humans. Practical prompt-injection research also exposed security weaknesses. BIPIA showed meaningful defensive progress before the post, so the evidence does not support a stronger claim that no narrow agent or defense could work reliably.
limitations: The result depends on interpreting the claim in its general-purpose device-agent context.
Benchmark failure rates are not universal deployment failure rates.
Effective bounded defenses existed; the security evidence does not establish impossibility.

our_interpretation: In context, 'that' means broadly capable LLM agents entrusted with autonomous actions across users' devices, rather than every narrow system called an AI agent.
The plain reading of reliable is dependable task execution with adequate resistance to malicious inputs. It does not mean perfect performance.

The observation concerns accumulated technical capability as of February 9, 2024. The target has no stated beginning; the latest public evaluations available by that date are used, without importing later improvements.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneously available evaluations show frequent failures on realistic multi-step tasks and unresolved security weaknesses relevant to broadly autonomous LLM agents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence available by the post shows broadly capable autonomous LLM agents executing realistic tasks dependably and maintaining effective security across the relevant threat surface.

evidence.explanation: The latest pre-post evaluation reports low success across realistic visual web tasks. This supports the lack of dependable broad task execution, although it does not test every possible agent design.

The study demonstrates practical attacks on LLM-integrated applications, including manipulation of API use and application behavior. It establishes a relevant security problem known before the post; later pre-post defensive progress must also be considered.

BIPIA reports strong defensive results for fine-tuned models in its tested tasks. This counters an absolute reading that the field knew no effective defenses, but does not establish secure, dependable general-purpose device agents.
